title: Learned three-gene score shows retrospective survival association in hepatitis-associated liver cancer
summary: CoxBoost combined with elastic-net regression formed a three-gene survival score for hepatitis-B-associated hepatocellular carcinoma. The paper reports survival separation in sixty TCGA and fifty-seven comparison-cohort samples. Both cohorts informed algorithm selection, limiting independent validation. The finding is a retrospective clinical association, without demonstrated treatment benefit or causal immune regulation.
ai_technology: CoxBoost and elastic-net regression for a three-gene survival-risk score

evidence.tested: The source selected sixty TCGA and fifty-seven HCCDB18 samples with clinical information. It compared 101 combinations of ten algorithms, using C-indices in both cohorts to choose CoxBoost plus elastic net with alpha 0.4. The learned score combined PARP1, KPNB1 and FARP2. Kaplan–Meier and time-dependent ROC analyses reported associations with observed overall survival in both cohorts.
evidence.unknown: The comparison cohort influenced model selection and is not an untouched external test. Small selected cohorts, incompletely reconstructed eligibility and outcome-informed comparisons limit generalization. Exact figure-level performance values were not independently transcribed. This record does not adopt predicted drug synergy, therapeutic reversal, causal immune effects or experimental biological claims.
evidence.ai_role: Boosted Cox learning and elastic-net fitting combined the three expression features into a risk score linked to measured patient survival. Univariate gene screening, generic enrichment and AI-agent drug suggestions alone are not the admitted result.

source_review.scope: Read primary clinical cohort acquisition, ten-algorithm/101-combination selection, CoxBoost/elastic-net evaluation Methods and survival-model Results. Operational biological procedures and drug claims were not processed or adjudicated. Figure-level numerical performance and supplements were not independently reconstructed. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
